_meta.title: Effects starter database
_meta.purpose: Function-to-effect mapping for TRIZ synthesis: given a required function, find candidate physical, chemical, or geometric effects that deliver it.
_meta.provenance: Curated from classical textbook physics, chemistry, and geometry (public-domain knowledge). Not extracted from proprietary TRIZ effect databases. Extend freely; verify application-specific constants, materials, and safety constraints from engineering references before use in a design.
_meta.usage: Served by the triz_effects MCP tool: list by category or search by function keywords. An effect states what a mechanism can do; selecting and substantiating it remains a synthesis and justification step, never a lookup verdict.

effects.name: Thermal expansion
effects.function: convert temperature change into displacement or force
effects.statement: Materials change dimension predictably with temperature; joined dissimilar metals bend when heated.
hints: shrink-fit assembly by heating or cooling

effects.name: Piezoelectric effect
effects.function: convert mechanical stress into voltage and back
effects.statement: Certain crystals generate charge when squeezed and deform when driven by voltage.

effects.name: Electromagnetic induction
effects.function: convert relative motion or field change between conductor and magnet into voltage
effects.statement: Moving a conductor through a magnetic field, or changing the field, induces an electromotive force.

effects.name: Resonance
effects.function: produce large amplitude from small periodic input
effects.statement: Driving a system at its natural frequency amplifies the response dramatically.

effects.name: Phase transition with latent heat
effects.function: store or release large amounts of heat at nearly constant temperature
effects.statement: Melting, freezing, evaporating, and condensing absorb or release large energy at a stable temperature.

effects.name: Evaporative cooling
effects.function: remove heat through vaporization of a liquid
effects.statement: A liquid taking its heat of vaporization cools its surroundings as it evaporates.

effects.name: Seebeck effect
effects.function: convert a temperature difference into electrical voltage
effects.statement: Two dissimilar conductors joined produce a voltage proportional to the temperature difference between their junctions.

effects.name: Peltier effect
effects.function: pump heat with electric current and no moving parts
effects.statement: Current through a semiconductor junction moves heat from one side to the other.

effects.name: Shape memory effect
effects.function: restore a trained shape by heating
effects.statement: A deformed shape-memory alloy returns to its set shape above a transition temperature, exerting force as it does.

effects.name: Superelasticity
effects.function: allow large reversible deformation with exact spring-back
effects.statement: Nitinol endures strains far beyond steel and returns exactly, via a stress-induced phase change.

effects.name: Curie point switching
effects.function: switch magnetism on and off with temperature
effects.statement: Ferromagnetic materials lose strong magnetization above a characteristic Curie temperature.

effects.name: Magnetostriction
effects.function: convert magnetic field into dimension change
effects.statement: Some materials stretch or contract slightly under magnetization.

effects.name: Electrostatic attraction
effects.function: create mechanical force from voltage between plates
effects.statement: Opposite charges on facing surfaces pull together with force growing with the square of the field.

effects.name: Hall effect
effects.function: sense magnetic field as a transverse voltage
effects.statement: Current in a conductor within a magnetic field develops a voltage across it proportional to the field.

effects.name: Photoelectric effect
effects.function: convert light into an electrical signal
effects.statement: Light above a threshold frequency frees charge carriers, producing a measurable current.

effects.name: Photoluminescence and phosphorescence
effects.function: absorb light energy and release it later or shifted in color
effects.statement: Phosphors store absorbed energy and re-emit it as visible light, immediately or with delay.

effects.name: Total internal reflection
effects.function: guide light inside a medium and detect surface contact
effects.statement: Light stays trapped by reflection at a boundary until the boundary condition changes.

effects.name: Interference
effects.function: measure nanometer-scale differences by superposing waves
effects.statement: Overlapping coherent waves create fringes that encode tiny path differences.

effects.name: Diffraction
effects.function: spread waves by geometry and encode structure in the pattern
effects.statement: Waves bend around features comparable to their wavelength; the resulting pattern reveals the feature.

effects.name: Polarization
effects.function: filter light by orientation and reveal stress fields
effects.statement: Light orientation survives certain filters, and stressed transparent materials rotate it.

effects.name: Doppler effect
effects.function: detect relative velocity from a frequency shift
effects.statement: Reflected waves shift frequency in proportion to the target's line-of-sight velocity.

effects.name: Coriolis effect
effects.function: measure mass flow or rotation rate from a rotating-frame force
effects.statement: Fluid in a vibrating tube twists it in proportion to mass flow; the same apparent force senses rotation rate.

effects.name: Gyroscopic effect
effects.function: resist reorientation of a spinning mass
effects.statement: A fast rotor responds to tilt with precession rather than yielding.

effects.name: Bernoulli effect
effects.function: generate low pressure where flow speeds up
effects.statement: Faster-moving fluid has lower static pressure and draws nearby material along.

effects.name: Coanda effect
effects.function: steer a fluid jet by giving it a surface to follow
effects.statement: A fluid jet attaches to an adjacent convex surface and follows its curve.

effects.name: Capillary action
effects.function: transport liquid passively through narrow geometry
effects.statement: Surface tension drives liquid into fine channels without external force.

effects.name: Osmosis
effects.function: move solvent selectively through a membrane
effects.statement: Solvent flows toward higher concentration across a semipermeable membrane.

effects.name: Diffusion
effects.function: transport species along a concentration gradient
effects.statement: Atoms and molecules spread from high to low concentration, faster at higher temperature.

effects.name: Ultrasonic vibration
effects.function: transmit force through material via high-frequency waves
effects.statement: Above-audible vibrations clean, join, cut, and sense inside opaque material.

effects.name: Acoustic levitation
effects.function: hold matter in standing waves without contact
effects.statement: Sound pressure nodes can trap small particles or droplets in mid-air.

effects.name: Cavitation
effects.function: concentrate energy locally by bubble collapse
effects.statement: Vapor bubbles formed in low-pressure zones collapse violently where pressure recovers.

effects.name: Adsorption
effects.function: capture molecules on a high-area surface
effects.statement: High-area surfaces bind target molecules from a gas or liquid.

effects.name: Corona discharge and ionic wind
effects.function: move air or particles with an electric field
effects.statement: A sharp high-voltage point ionizes air; the ions drag air along and charge particles for collection.

effects.name: Eddy currents
effects.function: induce braking, heating, or detection with changing magnetic fields
effects.statement: Time-varying magnetic fields drive circulating currents that oppose motion and dissipate energy.

effects.name: Superconductivity
effects.function: carry current without loss below a critical temperature
effects.statement: Zero resistance plus flux expulsion enables persistent currents and stable levitation.

effects.name: Catalysis
effects.function: accelerate a reaction without being consumed
effects.statement: A catalyst lowers activation energy and emerges unchanged.

effects.name: Exothermic reaction
effects.function: release heat on demand
effects.statement: Certain reactions release large heat once triggered.

effects.name: Endothermic reaction
effects.function: absorb heat on demand
effects.statement: Dissolving or reacting certain species pulls heat from the surroundings.

effects.name: Polymerization
effects.function: solidify liquid monomers into a solid in place
effects.statement: Liquid precursors cure into a solid polymer on demand.

effects.name: Sacrificial oxidation
effects.function: protect a structure by consuming a cheaper reactive material
effects.statement: A more reactive metal corrodes preferentially, sparing the structure it is connected to.

effects.name: Colorimetric reaction
effects.function: make chemical state visible as a color change
effects.statement: Reagents change color in the presence of a target species at low concentration.

effects.name: Chemiluminescence
effects.function: generate light from a reaction without external power
effects.statement: Some reactions emit light directly as they proceed.

effects.name: Hygroscopy
effects.function: absorb moisture from the environment
effects.statement: Certain materials take up water vapor, changing mass and mechanical properties as they do.

effects.name: Electroplating
effects.function: deposit metal from solution using current
effects.statement: Electric current reduces metal ions onto a conductive surface, building thickness layer by layer.

effects.name: Photopolymerization
effects.function: solidify resin only where light shines
effects.statement: Light cures a liquid resin locally and rapidly.

effects.name: Sublimation
effects.function: pass from solid directly to gas or deposit from gas to solid
effects.statement: Some solids vaporize without melting, and their vapor deposits as a solid elsewhere.

effects.name: Molecular sieve separation
effects.function: separate mixtures by molecular size and affinity
effects.statement: Engineered pores admit some molecules and exclude others.

effects.name: Combustion
effects.function: release energy rapidly by oxidation
effects.statement: Fuel plus oxidizer releases heat and rapid gas expansion.
hints: one-shot actuation such as explosive bolts

effects.name: Wedge and inclined plane
effects.function: trade distance for force along a slope
effects.statement: A slope converts a small force over long travel into a large force over short travel.

effects.name: Lever
effects.function: trade force for displacement about a pivot
effects.statement: Torque balance multiplies force by the ratio of lever arms.

effects.name: Screw helix
effects.function: convert rotation into linear motion with self-locking
effects.statement: The helix gains mechanical advantage and holds position under load.

effects.name: Gear ratio
effects.function: trade speed for torque exactly
effects.statement: Meshed gears exchange speed and torque by tooth count.

effects.name: Compliant flexure
effects.function: guide motion without joints or assemblies
effects.statement: Elastic geometry delivers repeatable motion with no play, backlash, or lubrication.

effects.name: Conic focus
effects.function: concentrate parallel energy to a point and back
effects.statement: A paraboloid focuses parallel rays to one point; an ellipse transfers focus to focus.

effects.name: Honeycomb and lattice
effects.function: maximize stiffness for minimal mass
effects.statement: Cellular cores carry shear and bending with very little material.

effects.name: Origami folding
effects.function: store a large surface in a small volume
effects.statement: Crease patterns let a sheet deploy into a designed three-dimensional shape.

effects.name: Vibration-assisted release
effects.function: release particles from a surface or remove a deposited layer by vibrating it
effects.statement: A vibrating surface accelerates what sits on it; particles and a brittle deposited layer detach once the inertial force, mass times peak acceleration, exceeds the adhesion holding them.
hints: vibratory bin activators that free sticking bulk solids
rapping heat-exchanger tubes to shed fouling

effects.name: Reverse-flow (back-pulse) cleaning
effects.function: remove a deposited layer from a porous surface or channel by reversing the flow through it
effects.statement: Drag and the pressure difference across a deposit point along the flow that built it up; a short pulse of reverse flow turns them around, lifting the deposited layer and carrying its particles away from the surface.
hints: backwashing granular media beds in water treatment
purging clogged sensing lines and nozzles

effects.name: Electrostatic repulsion
effects.function: release particles from a surface or keep them off it with like charges
effects.statement: Like charges repel with a force given by Coulomb's law: charging a surface and the particles on it to the same sign pushes the particles away.
hints: electrodynamic screens that sweep particles off solar panels and optics

effects.name: Thermal-expansion mismatch detachment
effects.function: remove a deposited layer or coating from a surface by heating or cooling it
effects.statement: A layer and its substrate with different expansion coefficients strain by different amounts when the temperature changes; the mismatch stress at the interface cracks the layer and peels it off.
hints: thermal-shock descaling of pipes and molds
cryogenic blasting that shrinks and embrittles coatings
releasing ice or wax by brief heating
